answer_1.quote: Due to high annotation costs, existing work proposes to synthesize target-domain QA pairs via neural question generation (QG) models.
answer_1.outputs: synthetic QA pairs (questions generated from contexts and answers)

answer_2.quote: We use the log likelihood scores of synthetic questions produced by the QG model (LM Score) as a metric to filter noisy questions.

answer_4.quote: To understand why QVE brings superior improvement, we conduct human evaluation and find that QVE can better identify semantically-matched and difficult questions. Three annotators work independently and we adopt the majority vote for deciding the final labels of a generated QA pair.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators labeled generated questions for semantic equivalence to ground truth and non-triviality (difficulty compared to human-created questions).
